sources.suppliedStrength: Primary Masonic constitutions (Regius Poem, Anderson’s 1723 Constitutions), Scottish Rite history, and Knights Templar historiography.

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (via Wikisource)
sources.suppliedDescription: Complete 11th Edition of the *Encyclopædia Britannica*, widely considered the pinnacle of pre-WWI classical, historical, and philological scholarship.
sources.suppliedStrength: Unfiltered pre-20th-century historiography on ancient mystery religions, secret societies, banking families, and comparative mythology before modern editorial compression.

sources.title: Forbidden Archeology / Michael Cremo Archive
sources.suppliedDescription: Research portal of Vedic scholar Michael Cremo documenting anomalous archaeological discoveries from 19th- and 20th-century scientific journals.
sources.suppliedStrength: Bibliographic citations of suppressed or ignored paleoanthropological artifacts challenging linear evolutionary chronology.

sources.title: Gegensatz Press / Savitri Devi Archive
sources.suppliedDescription: Archival repository preserving primary historical texts intersecting cyclic Hindu cosmology (*Yuga* theory), revisionist history, and 20th-century political esotericism.
sources.suppliedStrength: Complete primary texts examining how ancient Indo-European solar myths and cyclic time concepts were adapted by 20th-century ideological movements.

notes: Historical ideological material; contextualize author and claims accurately. Membership is not endorsement.

sources.title: Lacunae / Fortean & Anomalous History (Resologist / Charles Fort)
sources.suppliedDescription: Hypertext edition of all four of Charles Fort’s classic works (*The Book of the Damned*, *New Lands*, *Lo!*, *Wild Talents*).
sources.suppliedStrength: Thousands of cited 19th-century scientific journal and newspaper accounts of anomalous historical, astronomical, and physical phenomena excluded by orthodox science.

sources.title: Halexandria
sources.suppliedDescription: Expansive independent hypertext encyclopedia synthesizing revisionist ancient history, Sumerian/Babylonian mythology, sacred geometry, and suppressed science.
sources.suppliedStrength: High-density cross-linking between Mesopotamian cuneiform narratives, biblical revisionism, and hyperdimensional physics.

sources.title: Bibliotecapleyades
sources.suppliedDescription: Massive bilingual (English/Spanish) alternative research mega-archive compiling thousands of out-of-print books, articles, and essays on ancient history, secret societies, and geopolitics.
sources.suppliedStrength: Unrivaled breadth of archived essays on the Knights Templar, Jesuits, Black Nobility, Vatican finances, and Sumerian cosmology (requires strict source verification by the researcher).

sources.title: Institute of Noetic Sciences (IONS)
sources.suppliedDescription: Research institute founded by Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell conducting peer-reviewed experimental research on consciousness, psi phenomena, and mind-matter interaction.
sources.suppliedStrength: Open-access empirical papers by Dean Radin, Arnaud Delorme, and Helané Wahbeh on quantum wave-function collapse, telepathy, and non-local consciousness.

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: University of Virginia — Division of Perceptual Studies (DOPS)
sources.suppliedDescription: Academic medical school unit founded by Dr. Ian Stevenson investigating empirical evidence for consciousness surviving bodily death.
sources.suppliedStrength: Over 600 downloadable peer-reviewed academic papers on verified childhood past-life memories, near-death experiences (Bruce Greyson), and irreducible mind theory (Edward Kelly).

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: Essentia Foundation
sources.suppliedDescription: Academic and philosophical think tank founded by Bernardo Kastrup exploring analytic idealism—the metaphysical framework that consciousness is fundamental and matter is its extrinsic appearance.
sources.suppliedStrength: Rigorous philosophical and neuroscientific essays dismantling materialist physicalism through quantum foundations (Carlo Rovelli, Anton Zeilinger) and phenomenology.

sources.title: The Monroe Institute
sources.suppliedDescription: Research and educational organization founded by Robert Monroe pioneering binaural-beat hemispheric synchronization (Hemi-Sync) and out-of-body consciousness states.
sources.suppliedStrength: Primary documentation of Focus levels (Focus 10–27), EEG correlates of non-physical states, and the original source material for the CIA’s *Gateway Process* assessment.

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: Society for Psychical Research (SPR) / Psi Encyclopedia
sources.suppliedDescription: Peer-reviewed encyclopedia maintained by the London-based Society for Psychical Research (founded 1882 by Cambridge scholars).
sources.suppliedStrength: Over 600 scholarly articles detailing 140 years of rigorous experimental research into telepathy, precognition, psychokinesis, and mediumship.

sources.title: Journal of Transpersonal Psychology (ATP Archive)
sources.suppliedDescription: Official archive of the *Journal of Transpersonal Psychology*, founded in 1969 by Abraham Maslow, Stanislav Grof, and Anthony Sutich.
sources.suppliedStrength: Decades of open-access peer-reviewed papers on holotropic states, spiritual emergencies, psychedelic integration, and Ken Wilber’s perennial psychology.
sources.suppliedAccessModel: Free full-text PDFs for archival issues.

sources.title: Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies (MAPS)
sources.suppliedDescription: Leading research organization investigating the therapeutic, spiritual, and neurological mechanisms of psychedelics and entheogens.
sources.suppliedStrength: Thirty-five years of searchable *MAPS Bulletins*, clinical trial protocols, and Stanislav Grof / Ralph Metzner archival articles.

sources.title: Erowid
sources.suppliedDescription: Documenting the complex relationship between humans and psychoactive plants, chemicals, and endogenous visionary states.
sources.suppliedStrength: Archival Vaults containing complete writings and lectures of Terence McKenna, Alexander Shulgin, Albert Hofmann, R. Gordon Wasson (Eleusinian Mysteries), and John C. Lilly.

sources.title: ARAS (Archive for Research in Archetypal Symbolism)
sources.suppliedDescription: Pictorial and commentary archive grown out of the Eranos conferences (C.G. Jung, Mircea Eliade, Joseph Campbell, Henry Corbin) cataloging primordial symbols across human history.
sources.suppliedStrength: Jungian amplifications of cross-cultural motifs in alchemy, myth, ritual, and dream iconography.
sources.suppliedAccessModel: Free newsletter essays and public symbol portals; institutional/member login for full 18,000-image database.

sources.title: Center for Consciousness Studies (University of Arizona)
sources.suppliedDescription: Academic center directed by Stuart Hameroff hosting the biennial *Science of Consciousness* conferences.
sources.suppliedStrength: Primary abstracts and papers on Orch OR (Orchestrated Objective Reduction—quantum computations in brain microtubules developed with Roger Penrose) and panpsychism.
sources.suppliedAccessModel: Free abstract books and research papers.

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: David Bohm & J. Krishnamurti Archives (KFA / KFT)
sources.suppliedDescription: Complete text, audio, and video archive of Jiddu Krishnamurti’s dialogues, including his famous multi-year inquiries with quantum physicist David Bohm.
sources.suppliedStrength: Verbatim transcripts of the Bohm-Krishnamurti dialogues on *The Ending of Time*, the Implicate Order, psychological conditioning, and the nature of the observer.

sources.title: Rupert Sheldrake Official Research Archive
sources.suppliedDescription: Cambridge biochemist Rupert Sheldrake’s repository of peer-reviewed papers, experimental data, and essays on morphic resonance and extended mind.
sources.suppliedStrength: Full-text scientific papers on morphogenetic fields, the sense of being stared at, telepathy in biological systems, and the variability of fundamental physical constants.

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: Dean Radin / Consciousness Research Laboratory
sources.suppliedDescription: Curated bibliography and full-text repository of parapsychological meta-analyses and double-slit consciousness experiments.
sources.suppliedStrength: Direct links to peer-reviewed physics and psychology journal articles demonstrating statistically significant mind-matter interaction.

notes: Evaluate individual studies and replication; publication or institution alone does not establish the claimed phenomena.

sources.title: C.G. Jung Page / Jungian Studies Resources
sources.suppliedDescription: Long-standing independent portal hosting scholarly papers on analytical psychology, synchronicity, the *Red Book* (*Liber Novus*), and Gnostic-Jungian parallels.
sources.suppliedStrength: Deep commentary on Jung’s *Seven Sermons to the Dead*, *Answer to Job*, and *Mysterium Coniunctionis*.

sources.title: The Law of One (L/L Research)
sources.suppliedDescription: Complete, hyper-indexed database of the 106 sessions of the *Ra Contact* (1981–1984) conducted by physicist Don Elkins, Carla Rueckert, and Jim McCarty.
sources.suppliedStrength: Precision search engine (`lawofone.info`) indexing cosmology, density evolution, energy centers (chakras), Tarot archetypes, and polarity mechanics (Service-to-Others vs. Service-to-Self).

notes: Classify claims as attributed channelled/tradition material; do not recast them as empirical findings.

sources.title: Alexandria: Cosmology, Philosophy, Myth, and Culture
sources.suppliedDescription: Archive of the journal *Alexandria* edited by David Fideler, exploring the intersection of Neoplatonic cosmology, Hermeticism, and modern science.
sources.suppliedStrength: Scholarly essays by Kathleen Raine, Joscelyn Godwin, and Seyyed Hossein Nasr on the harmony of the spheres and sacred science.
sources.suppliedAccessModel: Free sample essays and archival indexes.

sources.title: PhilPapers (Philosophy of Mind & Metaphysics)
sources.suppliedDescription: Comprehensive index and open-access repository of academic philosophy maintained by the Center for Digital Philosophy.
sources.suppliedStrength: Exhaustive taxonomy of open-access preprints on panpsychism, cosmopsychism, dual-aspect monism (Pauli-Jung conjecture), and phenomenology.

sources.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (SEP)
sources.suppliedDescription: Peer-reviewed dynamic reference work maintained by Stanford University covering every major figure and school in Western and Eastern metaphysics.
sources.suppliedStrength: Authoritative bibliographic syntheses and technical breakdowns of Plotinus, Proclus, Ibn 'Arabi, Suhrawardi, Spinoza, and Quantum Consciousness.
